'''Percy Alec Deift''' (born September 10, 1945)<ref name="ams">{{cite journal | year = 2001 | title = Biographies of Candidates 2001 | url = https://www.ams.org/notices/200108/bios01.pdf | journal = [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] | volume = 48 | page = 8 }}</ref> is a mathematician known for his work on [[spectral theory]], [[integrable system]]s, [[random matrix|random matrix theory]] and [[Riemann–Hilbert problem]]s.

==Life==
Deift was born in Durban, [[South Africa]], where he obtained degrees in [[chemical engineering]], [[physics]], and [[mathematics]], and received a Ph.D. in [[mathematical physics]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1977.<ref>[https://math.nyu.edu/people/profiles/DEIFT_Percy.html Percy Deft, NYU Arts & Science]</ref> He is a Silver Professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], [[New York University]].

==Honors and awards==
Deift is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (elected 2012),<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (elected 2003),<ref>{{cite book |chapter= Alphabetical Index of Active Members |title= Bulletin of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences |date= Fall 2013 |chapter-url= https://www.amacad.org/multimedia/pdfs/alphalist.pdf}}</ref> and of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] (elected 2009).<ref>[http://www.nyu.edu/nyutoday/article/1804 Courant’s Percy Deift Elected to National Academy of Sciences], NYU Today, vol. 22 (2009), no. 11. Accessed January 13, 2010.</ref><ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200907/rtx090700844p.pdf Mathematics People], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 56 (2009), no. 7, p. 844</ref>

He is a co-winner of the 1998 [[Pólya Prize (SIAM)|Pólya Prize]],<ref name="ams"/><ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/199810/people.pdf SIAM Awards Pólya Prize], [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]],  vo. 45 (1998), no. 10, p. 1363</ref>
and was named a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1999.<ref name="ams"/><ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=d&page=6 Fellows list], {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100421200032/http://www.gf.org/fellows/all?index=d |date=2010-04-21 }} [[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]. Accessed January 13, 2010.</ref> He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited address at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin in 1998<ref name="ams"/><ref>[http://www.ms.unimelb.edu.au/~nsw/amsi2004/deift.html Professor Percy Deift] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304103639/http://www.ms.unimelb.edu.au/~nsw/amsi2004/deift.html |date=4 March 2016 }}, Integrable Systems, Rigorous Asymptotics and Applications Workshop, August 22–23, 2004, [[University of Melbourne]]. Accessed January 13, 2010</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Deift, P.|author2=Kriecherbauer, T.|author3=McLaughlin, K T.-R.|author4=Venakides, S.|author5=Zhou, X.|chapter=Uniform asymptotic for orthogonal polynomials|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=491–501|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011605000}}</ref> and plenary addresses in 2006 at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Madrid and at the [[International Congress on Mathematical Physics]] in Rio de Janeiro.<ref>[http://www.ms.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~yasuyuki/icmp2006.htm International Congress on Mathematical Physics - ICMP 2006]</ref> Deift gave the Gibbs Lecture at the Joint Meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2009.<ref>[http://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm/deift Deift to Deliver the Gibbs Lecture]</ref>  Along with [[Michael Aizenman]] and [[Giovanni Gallavotti]], he won the [[Henri Poincaré Prize]] in 2018.
